headline: A 2016 law names the federal courthouse in Greenville, North Carolina, after former judge Randy D. Doub.
what_it_does: The law gives the federal courthouse at 150 Reade Circle in Greenville, North Carolina, the official name "Randy D. Doub United States Courthouse." The name applies only while the building is used as a U.S. courthouse. The law does not change how the court operates or what cases it hears.
when_it_takes_effect: The law took effect on October 7, 2016, the date it was enacted.
